correctness.rationale: The Hardy–Weinberg marginal survivals give (1) and (2) with positive denominators. Positive post-pulse matrices with uniform entry bounds keep normalized densities away from the simplex boundary. The surviving mixing gap bounds the stagewise spread by successive decreases of the maximum susceptible fraction. A strictly selected stage rules out a common interior limit, and the initial maximum is below one. For h>0, late entrywise multiplicative sandwiches give both componentwise Perron exponents; strict Perron monotonicity and division by total density give the stated strictly negative log-rate. For h=0 the resistant recurrence is exactly linear. In (3), writing W_k=b_k u_k bounds the remainder by O(b_k^2), as the scaled resistant vector tends to a positive Perron vector and u_k is bounded. The normalized recurrence has an O(b_k) perturbation on the stable complement of the Perron projection, so u_k→v. The projected quadratic coefficient is S/a, since d_i(Ev)_i=ρ(M)v_i. The reciprocal increment tends to S/a and the factor a cancels when passing to fractions. Between pulses the fractions lie between the post-pulse minimum and maximum, giving both continuous-time limits, also at ρ(M)=1. Read the frozen proof, VERIFICATION.md and verify.py; did not run the supplied script. Its rational identities and finite two-stage tests are supplementary. Positivity of both initial alleles and deterministic fixed parameters are essential scope restrictions.

value.rationale: The endpoint rate is invisible to a linearized multiplier. Its exact coefficient shows how stage-specific selection is weighted over one period, distinguishes algebraic from exponential fixation, and separates both fraction asymptotics from baseline density growth.
